text:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up on cohort vs per-tenant micro-lanes for continuous batching. Capturing tradeoffs + next steps.
raj: Per-tenant lanes = strong isolation for p99 but hurts batching and KV locality. Cohorts = better GPU utilization, weaker isolation.
liam: GPUs need steady batches. Too many tiny lanes blow throughput.
sophia: KV-cache affinity is crucial; splitting reduces cache hits and spikes tail latency.
ana: Proposal: hybrid topology 1 micro-lanes for SLA-critical tenants, 3 cohorts for short/medium/long. Router uses (tenant_id, sla_tag, seq_len_hint).
raj: Need per-lane windowing, preemption policy, and cache-warm strategies.
liam: Runtime change: pass lane metadata into coalescer so it applies per-lane windows.
sophia: Observability required: per-lane p50/p95/p99, kv-hit-rate, batch-size CDF, fallback counts.
ana: Add hysteresis for cohort promotions (e.g., 20s sustained) to avoid oscillation.
maya: Sim plan: trace-replay with tenant mix, KV cold-starts, 3x load spike. Run before any rollout.
sophia: I'll extend harness to tag tenants and inject KV events.
liam: I'll spike coalescer changes and admission-credit model.
raj: Action items: observability matrix, router API sketch, admission pseudocode, simulation runs. Revisit in 48h.
sim-bot: Created sim job template under infra/batching/spikes/hybrid.
